literal: In hostility, triumphing is sweet, he who says, his life, failing and ruining, is near.
translation: The downfall and utter ruin of the life of one who thinks it is sweet to triumph in hostility are very near.
modern: மாறுபாட்டில் வெல்வது இனிமையானது என்று நினைப்பவனுடைய வாழ்க்கை, தவறிப் போவதும் அழிந்து போவதும் மிக அருகில் உள்ளன.
explanation: This couplet warns against the desire to dominate or triumph in a state of hostility. If a person believes that winning or asserting superiority in an ongoing feud is a sweet and desirable thing, their downfall is imminent. The poet uses two distinct terms, 'taval' (slipping or failing) and 'keṭal' (complete ruin), to show the stages of decline. The word 'naṇittu' emphasizes that this double disaster of slipping from one's position and being destroyed is not far off, but extremely close at hand.
